climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Chardonnay, Riesling, Sauvignon Blanc, Sémillon and Cabernet Franc fully without cooking off their freshness.
Chardonnay sits in its sweet spot, so the wines can show the style it is known for.
Pinot Noir is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Pinot Gris is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.

soil.rock: Volcanic rock is porous, so it drains well and sends roots deep. Lava soils are mostly basalt, rich in iron, calcium and magnesium.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.
